description: Gripper jaw wear and force inspection — PROC-53

box_1.text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect the gripper body for cracks, dents, or deformation at jaw mounting faces. 2. Check the actuator housing for impact damage or distortion. 3. Inspect the jaw slide channel for scoring or material loss.

box_2.text: Structural damage present on gripper body?

box_3.text: End, Escalate: structural damage, station offline

box_4.text: Using a calibrated depth gauge or digital micrometer, measure jaw insert thickness at three equally spaced points along the contact face. Record the minimum value and compare it against the minimum serviceable thickness in the jaw service specification. Note whether wear is concentrated at the part contact zone or distributed evenly, as concentrated wear indicates jaw misalignment during clamping.

box_6.text: Replace jaw inserts, symmetric replacement, both jaws

box_7.text: Reverify jaw geometry after insert replacement

box_8.text: End, Part rejected: jaw geometry non conforming after replacement

box_9.text: Mount a calibrated dynamometer between the closed jaw faces with the instrument aligned along the grip axis. Command the chuck to apply nominal clamping pressure and record the force reading. Repeat the test at 50% and 100% of the programmed grip pressure, then compare both readings against the minimum and maximum grip force values in the fixture specification.

box_11.text: Adjust gripper actuator pressure to rated value

box_12.text: Reverify gripping force after pressure adjustment

box_13.text: End, Escalate: gripper actuator replacement required

box_14.text: Load the designated reference part into the fixture under normal clamping pressure. Using a dial test indicator, measure part position at the primary datum face and at the two secondary locating surfaces. Record all three readings and compare against the permitted positional tolerance stated in the fixture qualification record.

box_15.text: Refer to the jaw positional tolerance specification.

box_17.text: Realign jaw mounting using precision alignment jig

box_18.text: With the fixture open, visually inspect the jaw pivot pins and guide rails for dry running, corrosion, or swarf accumulation. Apply a thin film of the specified grease to each pivot pin and run the jaw through three full open and close cycles to distribute lubricant evenly. Wipe away any excess from the part contact surfaces.

box_19.text: Refer to the gripper lubrication specification.

box_21.text: Apply lubricant to pivot pins per lubrication chart

box_22.text: Log maintenance and update maintenance management system service record

box_24.text: Second jaw alignment attempt: adjust the jaw mounting screws in quarter turn increments in the direction that reduces the measured error. Run the jaw through three full open and close cycles to allow the inserts to seat, then remeasure jaw geometry at all three measurement points with the depth gauge before returning to the geometry verification step.
